core_obligations: Show that the extension property for all ideals implies the extension property for all submodules, by taking a maximal counterexample and reducing to a cyclic extension (proof lines 13703-13740).
Verify the extension property in the remaining case by an explicit construction using the annihilator of the element that generates the cyclic extension (proof lines 13740-13755).
Conclude the characterisation stated in the lemma (proof lines 13755-13756).
proof_roadmap: Reduce the general extension property to the case of ideals (proof lines 13703-13720).
Use a maximal counterexample to reduce to a cyclic extension (proof lines 13720-13740).
Construct the extension explicitly and conclude (proof lines 13740-13756).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a characterisation of injectivity for modules over a ring in terms of ideals, and the proof is a 54-line argument that follows the classical route of Baer's criterion. It shows first that the extension property for all ideals implies the extension property for all inclusions by passing to a maximal counterexample and reducing to the case of a cyclic extension, and then verifies the criterion in the case that matters by an explicit construction with the annihilator of an element. The reduction to the maximal counterexample and the explicit extension are both written out.
